body_systems.label: Heart and circulation
body_systems.function: Pumps blood and oxygen to every organ. In weightlessness fluid shifts toward the head and the heart works differently.

body_systems.label: Lungs and breathing
body_systems.function: Take in oxygen and remove CO2. In a closed cabin CO2 can build up around you in still air.

body_systems.label: Brain, sleep and mood
body_systems.function: Attention, mood and sleep. Isolation, confinement and a shifted day-night cycle wear them down.

body_systems.label: Bones and muscles
body_systems.function: Carry and move the body. Without gravity they lose mass unless loaded by exercise.
body_systems.summary: Exercise heart rate is stable for the same exercise types.

body_systems.label: Blood and metabolism
body_systems.function: Carries sugar, fluid and salts. Fluid loss and irregular meals show up here first.

body_systems.label: Immune system and radiation
body_systems.function: Defends against infection. Radiation and stress weaken it, and a closed cabin spreads germs.
body_systems.summary: Radiation dose rate is 4.1 times the 7-day normal and has been elevated for 19 hours.

body_systems.label: Eyes
body_systems.function: In weightlessness fluid shifts toward the head; in some astronauts the optic disc swells and near vision changes (SANS).
body_systems.summary: The optic disc margin is 28% less sharp than in your baseline photo: an early sign to watch. The photo goes to your flight surgeon in today's report.

body_systems.label: Kidneys and urine
body_systems.function: Filter the blood. Bone loss in space puts extra calcium in the urine, which raises the risk of kidney stones.

body_systems.label: Digestion
body_systems.function: Digests food and absorbs water. Space food, less movement and less fluid change bowel habits.

actions.action: Solar storm in progress: go to the storm shelter now.
Abort any EVA or rover traverse and return to the habitat.
Log your dosimeter reading when you enter and when you leave the shelter.
Your flight surgeon has been notified; stay sheltered until the dose rate is below the elevated level.
Radiation is elevated: stop EVA preparation and check that the storm shelter is clear and stocked.
Keep your dosimeter on and stay away from thinly shielded areas until the rate is back to normal.
Check your near vision with the eye chart in the medical kit and log any blurring or headache.
Retake the fundus photo in 7 days, same camera settings.
Your eye photo and baseline photo go to your flight surgeon in today's report.
